A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DoRA research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable matching; the checklist omitted from v4 is an actual document change.

before.justification: v2 reports original alignment experiments on HH-RLHF, summarization and UltraFeedback, including benchmark results, ablations, reward-model evaluations and an appendix comparison with RSO.

after.justification: v4 reports original alignment experiments and supplementary analyses, including label-corruption and iterative self-training results in Section 4.3.

M1.justification: The classifiers, calibration mechanism, robust objective and Algorithm 1 are retained. The expanded explanation of the class-imbalance ratio clarifies the existing method; the self-training experiment applies it in another setting.

E1.justification: The datasets and dialogue, summarization and instruction-following tasks are retained. Section 4.3 extends conditions within this coverage through label-corrupted training evaluated on HH-RLHF and AlpacaEval 2, and evolving self-generated training data on HH-RLHF.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same pairwise baselines, RobustDPO, Dr.DPO, listwise baselines and RSO. The added corruption and self-training experiments reuse DPO-PL, RRHF and LIRE.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds two distinct evaluation designs: random label flipping at 20%, 40% and 60% for HH-RLHF and 40% for AlpacaEval 2; and LLaMA-3.2-3B training on HH followed by two iterations using its own responses. Existing benchmark settings in Appendix C are retained.

E4.justification: New Tables 5 and 6 directly test robustness to corrupted labels and continued training on self-generated data. These substantially extend the robustness analyses beyond the retained calibration, robustness-parameter, component-ablation, convergence and qualitative analyses.

E5.justification: Removing the checklist deletes v2's statement that Table 1 error bars reflect multiple runs and that evaluation costs restricted their coverage. The same uncertainty values remain in Table 1, while the new tables provide no uncertainty estimates or repeated-run information.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial results for the two new evaluation designs. For example, Table 5 reports HH win rates of 57.3 for DPO-PL and 60.8 with DoRA at 60% corruption; Table 6 reports third-iteration DPO-PL scores of 85.0 and 88.0 with DoRA. These are newly reported settings; matched pre-existing results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Definition 2.1, Propositions 3.1–3.2 and Appendix B's derivations and convergence analysis are retained. Writing the existing class-imbalance ratio explicitly clarifies its meaning without substantively changing the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statement and conclusion retain the same claims about classifier-calibrated robust alignment under mixture response shifts. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds a substantive applicability limitation when the target distribution cannot be reliably estimated. It also replaces the offline-only limitation with a need for broader online validation. Section 4.3 interprets self-training results as evidence that calibration can handle evolving synthetic distributions.

D1.justification: The omitted checklist contained an explicit disclosure that the codebase was unfinished and release was planned; v4 provides no replacement access information. Appendix C retains the hardware, hyperparameters, data-generation settings, decoding settings and evaluation prompts.

R1.justification: v4 adds Liu et al.'s works on stable adversarial learning and describing distribution shifts, and removes Duchi and Namkoong's uniform-performance DRO reference. The substantive positioning against pairwise robustness approaches and RSO remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds Section 4.3 and acknowledgments, revises the limitations and class-imbalance explanation, moves the loss discussion from C.6 to D.1, and removes the checklist. The remaining scientific narrative and section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds two tables, refines Table 3's headers and places Figure 7 beside its discussion instead of on a separate page. Existing figure graphics are unchanged; other differences mainly involve local table formatting, reflow and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added corruption and self-training tests provide useful direct evidence for robustness beyond v2's experiments, and the target-distribution limitation better qualifies applicability. The improvement is limited by terse reporting of the new protocols, an unnamed metric in Table 6, and removal of the multiple-run and pending-code-release disclosures. The central method, theory and existing results remain unchanged.
